latest_nl_proof:
Fix a prime p > 5 with p ≡ 3 (mod 8), and let S = { k in {1,...,p-2} : I(k+1) < I(k) }.

I will prove the stronger estimate |S| >= (p-5)/2.

For each e in {1,...,p-2}, define
k_e := I(e+1) - 1.
Because I is a permutation of {1,...,p-1} and I(1)=1, it permutes {2,...,p-1}; hence e -> k_e is a bijection from {1,...,p-2} onto {1,...,p-2}.

Now I(k_e+1) = I(I(e+1)) = e+1.
It remains to compute I(k_e). Modulo p,
k_e = I(e+1)-1 ≡ (e+1)^(-1) - 1 ≡ -e(e+1)^(-1).
Therefore
k_e^(-1) ≡ -(e+1)e^(-1) ≡ -1 - e^(-1) (mod p).
Since e != p-1 and I is injective with I(p-1)=p-1, we have I(e) != p-1; thus p-1-I(e) lies in {1,...,p-2}. Also
p-1-I(e) ≡ -1 - e^(-1) ≡ k_e^(-1) (mod p).
By uniqueness of inverses in {1,...,p-1},
I(k_e) = p-1-I(e).
Hence
k_e in S
iff I(k_e+1) < I(k_e)
iff e+1 < p-1-I(e)
iff e + I(e) < p-2.
Because e -> k_e is a bijection, we get
|S| = #{ e in {1,...,p-2} : e + I(e) < p-2 }.   (1)

Now set
T := { e in {1,...,p-1} : e + I(e) < p }.
For every e in {1,...,p-1}, we have I(p-e)=p-I(e), because
(p-e)(p-I(e)) ≡ e I(e) ≡ 1 (mod p),
and p-I(e) is in {1,...,p-1}. Therefore
(p-e) + I(p-e) = 2p - (e + I(e)).
So, provided e + I(e) != p, exactly one of e and p-e belongs to T.

I claim that e + I(e) = p has no solution. Indeed, if e + I(e) = p, then I(e)=p-e, so
e(p-e) ≡ 1 (mod p),
hence -e^2 ≡ 1 (mod p), i.e. e^2 ≡ -1 (mod p). But p ≡ 3 (mod 4) (because p ≡ 3 (mod 8)), so this is impossible: if e^2 ≡ -1, then by Fermat's little theorem,
1 ≡ e^(p-1) = (e^2)^((p-1)/2) ≡ (-1)^((p-1)/2) = -1 (mod p),
a contradiction since (p-1)/2 is odd.
Thus no e satisfies e + I(e)=p.

Hence each pair {e, p-e} contributes exactly one element to T. There are (p-1)/2 such pairs, so
|T| = (p-1)/2.   (2)

Also p-1 is not in T, since I(p-1)=p-1 and (p-1)+I(p-1)=2p-2 > p. So T is really a subset of {1,...,p-2}.

Comparing (1) with T: the only elements of T not counted in (1) are those with
e + I(e) = p-1 or e + I(e) = p-2.
The case e + I(e) = p-2 is impossible, because then I(e)=p-2-e, so
e(p-2-e) ≡ 1 (mod p),
which gives
-e^2 - 2e ≡ 1 (mod p),
so (e+1)^2 ≡ 0 (mod p), hence e ≡ -1 (mod p), i.e. e = p-1, contradicting e in {1,...,p-2}.

The case e + I(e) = p-1 is equivalent to
I(e)=p-1-e,
so
e(p-1-e) ≡ 1 (mod p),
which is
e^2 + e + 1 ≡ 0 (mod p).
This quadratic congruence has at most 2 solutions modulo the prime p.
Therefore, from (2),
|S| >= |T| - 2 = (p-1)/2 - 2 = (p-5)/2.

Finally, write p = 8m+3 with m >= 1. Then
(p-5)/2 = 4m-1 >= 2m = floor(p/4).
So |S| >= floor(p/4), as required.
role_in_parent: Handles the second residue class modulo 8 with no need for the false arithmetic identity rejected earlier.
statement_nl: Let p be a prime number with p > 5 and p ≡ 3 (mod 8). For each k in {1,2,...,p-1}, let I(k) be the unique integer in {1,2,...,p-1} such that k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p), and define S = { k in {1,2,...,p-2} : I(k+1) < I(k) }. Then |S| >= floor(p/4).

domain_restrictions: p is a prime integer with p > 5
k ranges over integers 1 through p-1 when defining I(k); S is a subset of 1 through p-2 so I(k+1) is always defined
I(k) is taken as the unique representative in {1,...,p-1} (i.e. residues modulo p are represented by 1..p-1, not 0)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every prime integer p with p > 5 and p ≡ 3 (mod 8), define the map I_p: {1,...,p-1} → {1,...,p-1} by I_p(k) ≡ k^{-1} (mod p) with the representative chosen in {1,...,p-1}. Let S_p = { k ∈ {1,...,p-2} : I_p(k+1) < I_p(k) }. Then the cardinality satisfies |S_p| ≥ floor(p/4).
quantifier_order: for all p (p is a prime) with p > 5 and p ≡ 3 (mod 8)
for all k in {1,...,p-1}: define I(k) as the unique element of {1,...,p-1} with k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p)
define S = { k in {1,...,p-2} | I(k+1) < I(k) }

variables.name: p
variables.role: parameter; the prime for which the statement is asserted; constrained by p > 5 and p ≡ 3 (mod 8)

variables.name: k
variables.role: ranging/index variable used to define I(k) and to form S

variables.name: I
variables.role: defined function giving the multiplicative inverse representative: I(k) is the unique element of {1,..,p-1} with k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p)

variables.name: S
variables.role: defined set S = { k ∈ {1,..,p-2} | I(k+1) < I(k) } whose cardinality is bounded below

witness_dependencies: I(k) depends on both p and k: I = I_{p} with I_{p}(k) the multiplicative inverse modulo p represented in {1,..,p-1}
S depends on p via I: S = S_{p} = { k ∈ {1,..,p-2} | I_{p}(k+1) < I_{p}(k) }
the cardinality bound |S| ≥ floor(p/4) is a statement about S_{p} and thus depends only on p (through I)
